name: Nefiracetam
lead: Nefiracetam (code DM-9384) is an oral racetam-class nootropic studied mainly in Japan for dementia and post-stroke apathy.[1] It is not approved in the United States, where it is unscheduled, and it is prescription-only in Australia.[1]
Sources reviewed do not connect it to physical appearance.

paras: Laboratory studies reported enhancement of neuronal calcium channel currents,[2] modulation of acetylcholine receptor currents,[3] and increased turnover of GABAergic components in rat cortex.[4] It reduced amyloid-induced learning impairment in rats.[5]

A phase 2 trial in Alzheimer's disease (n=50) was registered in 1999.[6] Wikipedia describes preliminary studies in post-stroke apathy and in Alzheimer's-type and cerebrovascular dementia.[1] No study has examined appearance outcomes.
In animals, renal and testicular toxicity was seen, particularly in dogs, attributed to a metabolite that humans do not form; no toxicity was reported in clinical trials.[1]

quick.overview:
Nefiracetam is a racetam studied for dementia and apathy after stroke. It is sold online as a nootropic.

No source links it to appearance.
quick.mechanism: Lab studies point to effects on calcium channels, acetylcholine receptors and the GABA system.
quick.risks: Animal toxicity (kidney, testis) was seen in dogs; human trials reported none. Prescription-only in Australia.
